## What this lands

- **One audited restricted-byte access function** — `ops.restricted_access.audited_read`: writes a `sig.restricted-access/1` record (requester, purpose, time, object) under `ops/access-log/` BEFORE returning bytes — a failed fetch stays audited; an empty requester/purpose refuses, so no unaudited read exists.
- **Scheduled purge of expired log rows** — `sig-ops restricted-access purge` + the weekly `sig-access-log-purge` job: deletes only provably-expired records (180 d, SIG-EVID-012), keeps+flags what it can't parse, audits itself with `sig.access-log-purge/1`.
- **GCS Data Access audit logs + exclusion filter + retention sink** — `storage.googleapis.com` `DATA_READ`/`DATA_WRITE` folded into the project `auditConfigs` with `sig-ingest-rt`/`sig-export-rt`/`sig-replica-rt` exempted (G1-13's volume control); `sig-data-access` routes to PRIVATE `sig-audit-logs` under a 90-day delete lifecycle; the log-volume alert fires at the +$5/mo bound (FEA-18); the cost read runs before and after.
- **Cloud SQL ENCRYPTED_ONLY** — `sig-pg --ssl-mode=ENCRYPTED_ONLY` (G1-14), restore = the captured pre-state.
- **ADR-232** — the decision record + spec_src row + spec rebuild + index + ADR_TRIGGERS row.
- **The acceptance shape, fixture-verified** — a restricted read appears in the audit log (log-first ordering pinned by test).
